blocks.text: Quito and the Middle of the World

After breakfast, transfer to Quito’s historic centre, one of the largest and best-preserved colonial centres in Latin America.

The first stop is the Basilica of the National Vow, a neo-Gothic church whose decorations depict Ecuadorian animals in place of traditional European gargoyles. Continue to Independence Square, surrounded by the Presidential Palace, the Archbishop’s Palace, municipal buildings and the cathedral.

Next, visit La Compañía Church, whose interior is richly decorated with gold leaf. Then see San Francisco Square and the large 16th-century church and monastery complex known as the “Escorial of the Andes”.

The group then heads up El Panecillo, a hill topped by a statue of the Winged Virgin Mary. From here you can look out over Quito and the surrounding Andes.

In the afternoon, continue to the Middle of the World, about 22 km north of Quito. The equator line here was determined in the 18th century by the French Geodesic Mission in collaboration with Spanish and Ecuadorian geographers. The Intiñan Museum offers interactive experiments about being on the equator.

Return to the hotel in the evening.
A twin-towered neo-Gothic basilica rising above the neighbourhoods of Quito, Ecuador
Quito: the basilica’s pointed towers against a hillside covered in buildings

After breakfast, leave at 8:00 a.m. with a certified mountain guide. Take the cable car up to Cruz Loma station at around 4,000 m.

From here, start hiking along the edge of the mountain. The first section leads to the foot of Rucu Pichincha, followed by a long ascent to the summit at 4,696 m.

At the summit there’s time to rest and take photos. Then descend to the cable car and head back towards Quito. In the afternoon, transfer to Machachi.
